claim: With a dynamic gate, the core on the real wiring lowers held-out loss compared with the same core on an empty graph (same cell types, no edges), i.e. the dynamic-gate gain depends on the connectome and is not just an input-dependent adapter.

protocol.notes: 3,000-type subgraph (synapse-mass core + proportional inputs/outputs; 629,875 edges): the per-token persistent scan costs ~4x a reset step, which the full graph cannot afford here. 2 of every 8 rows are synthetic temporal-memory rows (recall at a distance, pattern, count, first item) in every arm.

notes: The dynamic-gate effect was first seen in the exploratory X-CNS-001 run (seed 1: pooled -0.0077 nats/char, temporal 6.78 -> 2.60) before this file was written; seed 1 is therefore excluded and the confirmation uses seeds 2-4. Same protocol as H-CNS-003 / X-CNS-001 (3,000-type subgraph, learned Dale edges, 250 core-only steps). With no edges the output types see only their bias, so the core's write is a learned constant and the dynamic gate turns it into a pure 320->320 tanh adapter: the matched no-connectome control. In the empty arm the output-type biases start at +0.1 (connectome_lab.EMPTY_OUT_BIAS; all other initial values equal the real arm's at the same seed, and the gate still starts at 0): at bias 0 the relu output types are silent and receive no gradient, which a pre-lock smoke run showed makes the control untrainable. Threshold 0.25% of the control (~0.001 nats/char, about 5-10 paired SDs; the graph-dependent part of the static core's gain was ~0.0015).
